metadata.notes: These 366 provisional research selections are not 366 verified stories. Source-led discovery and editor approval are separate. No published copy or unpublished graphics included.
metadata.summary: Pass14: 246/366 primary cores, 120 gaps, 27 new claim checks and zero approvals; weather history segment cautions retained.

limitations: All 366 dates have provisional primary/alternate IDs, not publication-ready vetted stories.
NCEI county/zone records can represent portions of multiday or multijurisdictional events; never sum without verification.
NHC best-track points without local geography/impact evidence are not valid as confirmed landfalls.
Curation quality and Tier 3 labels require human meteorologist editorial judgment.
Most events lack independent corroboration; international and pre-1950 coverage are particularly weak.
No image rights have been cleared in this Phase A research database.
Two sources may originate from the same institution; judge organizational independence separately.
Pass 2 screened two alternate records for each upgraded date (30 leads) but did not independently corroborate those alternate stories.
Same-institution corroboration is labeled and does not establish fully independent sourcing.

25 January 1990 Royal Meteorological Society and Met Office accounts share an underlying Met Office observation record; organizational separation does not mean independent gust measurement corroboration.
28 January 1887 giant-snowflake account held as unresolved historical-date/measurement issue, not upgraded.
Pass 2 continuation to 26 cases retains 8 prior alternate pairs unchanged; no additional independent alternate research is counted in 30 earlier screened leads.
Some dates refer to start of multiday episodes, a transportation closure, or streamflow peak windows rather than a whole-storm culmination. Per-claim dates require human review.
2021 NSW PDF statement text was retrieved but its rendered page could not be inspected; specific map panels and image rights remain unverified.
Great Storm of 1703 assigned Dec 7 in modern Gregorian anniversary, corresponding to November 26 Old Style (Julian); original contemporaneous documents must preserve source calendars.
Flight 242 FAA retelling relies on original NTSB investigation; Wilma NHC and WPC are both NOAA; neither pair is independent underlying event data.
Sept 30, 2019 Montana snow graphic NASA satellite was taken October 1 and snowfall totals refer to several days; source image never treated as September 30 same-day imagery.
Three newly upgraded dates cause or neighbor winter/fire/severe-weather clusters, recorded as editorial diversity warnings, not suppressions.
11 previous pairs of unverified alternates were retained without independent screening; earlier count of 30 screened alternate leads is unchanged.
1928 Okeechobee anniversary Sep 17 describes overnight surge/levee impacts from storm crossing evening Sep 16; never misidentify Sep 17 as Palm Beach coastal landfall.
2017 Hurricane Nate first local landfall Oct 7 near Mississippi River mouth, second landfall after midnight Oct 8 near Biloxi; these must remain distinct.
2014 Dec12 California atmosphere-river editorial hook is downstream high flow/river crest, not the Dec11 maximum onset rain period.
2017 Los Angeles Skirball Fire LAFD response time and CAL FIRE incident start time differ in source metadata; do not call them identical ignition moments.
Four tropical primary upgrades add legitimate historical stories but require subsequent consecutive-day hazard diversity review; do not optimize away higher impact facts automatically.
The former Tier 3 backlog is empty because replacements were given core occurrence/date corroboration, NOT because all primaries are fully source verified, fact checked, or approved.
August 9 2022 Seoul flood source pair shares Yonhap as publisher and underlying KMA rain reports. Treat as non-independent pending direct KMA validation.
August 15 2023 Yellowknife alert is for specific western neighborhoods only; city-wide evacuation followed August 16.
November 3 2007 Noel's extratropical transition and entry into Canadian responsibility region differ from subsequent November 4 Nova Scotia landfall.
October 22 2012 Sandy genesis selected instead of second consecutive Witch Creek fire narrative; original 2007 Witch Creek Oct 21 is preserved.
The May27–29 triple tornado clustering was broken earlier by the May28 Arkansas flood primary; all retain approval restrictions.
2 of 732 alternates now have core source corroboration on Aug27, leaving 730 unverified; common source data does NOT establish independent meteorological measurement.

Pass 3 corroborated 15 flagship event/date broad identities, but NCEI tornado segments and WFO summary pages often originate in the SAME NWS damage survey. A source URL is not independent weather observation evidence.
May28 2019 Fort Smith river stage exceeding its prior record does NOT mean May28 was the final flood peak; finalized 2019 Arkansas River crests occurred later at several stations.

May27-29 primary tornado repetition was reduced by replacing the May28 Linwood tornado with the Arkansas River flood. Original Linwood case remains a preserved research alternative; no alternates were newly independently screened.

Pass5 date pitfalls: Idai March15 only in Mozambique civil time; Bangladesh cyclone spans Apr29–30; Ahr downstream crests Jul15 after Jul14 heavy rain; 1913 Lake Huron winds/waves are modeled retrospectives, not contemporary observations.
1883 Krakatau eruption is selected for barometric wave forcing, not volcanic tsunami mislabeled as storm surge. Pre-instrument 1780 hurricane wind estimates are uncertain.
Pass 6: Feb 2, 2007 operational EF-scale transition means NCEI old 'F3' prose should not override finalized survey classification.
Pass 6: 2011 El Reno EF5 and 2013 El Reno tornado are different storms; measured Mesonet gusts and survey-inferred maxima are separate.
Pass 6: July27 2022 Kentucky marks intense evening rain onset and July28 the peak impacts; NASA Aug8 Maui weather reanalysis and fire ignition causality must not be conflated.
The 2011 Indiana State Fair case's old NWS event-detail link returned 404; date supported by Indiana state chronology and NWS year-index, with numerical gust/engineering findings pending.
Pass 7: Jan6 1839 Big Wind overnight peak extends into Jan7; 1993 Braer estimated cyclone center is not a land station pressure record.

Pass 7: Feb12 1899 historic Gulf Coast cold and snow spans Feb12–13, with minima at stations on different dates. Feb12 2006 NYC snowfall 'record' was valid then but must not be claimed current without updated climate ranking.
Pass 7: Halloween 1991 Upper Midwest blizzard and northwest Atlantic Perfect Storm are separate cyclones, not a single causal storm. The Atlantic system reached peak intensity Oct30, not Oct31.
Pass 7: Feb12 Oroville spillway threat resulted in evacuations, NOT a dam breach or measured downstream catastrophic flood; incident is a weather-driven hydrologic/engineering alternative only.
Pass 7: 2012 I-75 smoke-fog, 2022 I-57 fog, and 2021 Fort Worth I-35W crashes require careful distinction between weather conditions, human actions and proximate crash causation.
Pass13: the October31 Halloween 1991 blizzard is already a primary; a November1 repeat was rejected in favor of Typhoon Goni.
Pass13: June4 D-Day delay vs June6 landing, Czech IF4 vs EF4, October24 Yutu forecast vs October25 local landfall, and early Dorian vs final landfall bulletin must remain distinct.
Pass14: Audrey landfall category/time differ by source; Enderlin rating updated EF4 to EF5; 1940 Tacoma bridge collapse caused by aeroelastic flutter rather than simply high wind speed.

Pass14: North Carolina April16 separate parallel EF2/EF3 tracks, Nov21 LA F2 vs MS F1, Nov20 2022 South Bend 30.2-inch calendar-month-to-date total, Dec25 Devore and Waterman Canyon site distinctions.
revision_workflow: Preserve manually curated events and all existing Post Studio copy.
Check source link and dated claims, then independently corroborate before selecting verified status.
Replace weak primary stories with stronger dated events, including international and early historical candidates.
Review every low-quality or same-source-repetition warning; seek non-NOAA primary research sources.
Do not mark approved until full human review and image rights checks are complete.
